Cathie Wood Just Sold $5 Million of Spotify © Africa images via Canva
Key Takeaways

Cathie Wood's ARK Invest sold 8,961 shares of Spotify from one ETF on Friday, worth about $5.2 million at Friday's close.

Analysts expect Spotify's normalized EPS to nearly double from 2025 to 2028, and the stock trades below its average forward P/E since 2024.

Warner Music Group's subscription streaming growth sped up to 15% on higher per-subscriber minimums, and those minimums are a cost for Spotify.

The numbers don't back the sale, so I'd hold, and Spotify's early-February report is the next test.

Cathie Wood's ARK Invest sold 8,961 shares of Spotify (SPOT:NYSE) on Friday, according to ARK's daily trade email. At Friday's close of $577.03, that's about $5.2 million.

The sale came a day after Warner Music Group (WMG:NASDAQ), one of the biggest labels Spotify licenses music from, reported a quarter that shows how much the labels are getting out of streaming's price rises. What's good for Warner is a cost for Spotify.

One ETF, and a sliver of it

All 8,961 shares came out of the ARK Next Generation Internet ETF (ARKW), and ARK's email puts them at 0.14% of the ETF. The $5.2 million is worked out as shares times Friday's close, because the email doesn't say what ARK got for them. The email also lists only the portfolio adjustments ARK's team made that day, so it may leave some trades out.

ARK manages about $17.4 billion. Its 13F for the quarter ended Sept. 30, filed Nov. 13, lists 181 US stock positions. A day's email doesn't say why ARK sold or how much Spotify it still holds. What it does show is a small sale from one fund.

TIKR tracks 41 analysts on Spotify. How many say "Buy"?

See the full breakdown of Buy, Hold, and Sell ratings on Spotify, along with Wall Street's revenue and earnings estimates, all in one place. More than 500,000 investors use TIKR to research stocks like this one. See Spotify's Analyst Ratings

The earnings keep climbing

Analysts expect Spotify's normalized EPS to rise every year through 2028:

Spotify Technology (SPOT): normalized EPS, actual and consensus estimates, $ per share, fiscal 2023-2028 (TIKR)

That's growth of about 13% in 2026, 28% in 2027 and 26% in 2028, which takes EPS close to double 2025's level. The 2026 increase looks small because Spotify paid almost no tax on its 2025 earnings, helped by a deferred tax benefit. Analysts expect an effective tax rate of about 22% this year.

The business underneath is still heading the right way. Third-quarter revenue rose 16% to €4.97 billion and gross margin reached 33.0%. Management guides fourth-quarter operating income to €820 million, up 17% from a year earlier.

Spotify also isn't priced like a company growing this fast. At 37x forward earnings, it trades below the roughly 48x it averaged at quarter-ends from March 2024 through September 2026, and not far above its 31x low in June 2026.

Spotify Soars 12.5% in a Month as the Nasdaq Slides. Its CFO Still Targets a 20%+ Operating Margin by 2030 ©@twinsterphoto via Canva; @Adam Smigielski from Getty Images Signature via Canva
Key Takeaways

Spotify stock is up 12.5% in the past month as the Nasdaq 100 fell, on a third quarter that beat guidance.

Warner Music Group, still negotiating over Spotify's planned AI remix add-on, is sharing in streaming price increases.

CFO Christian Luiga reaffirmed a 20%-plus operating margin target for 2030, against 12.8% in 2025.

Spotify trades below its usual multiple, a buy if the fourth quarter delivers 10 million net adds and a 16% operating margin.

Spotify Technology (SPOT:NYSE) stock is up 12.5% in the past month on a strong quarter and a planned AI add-on. Meanwhile, the Nasdaq 100 fell 10%.

On Nov. 19, CFO Christian Luiga told Morgan Stanley's conference that Spotify still aims for an operating margin above 20% by 2030. The same day, record label Warner Music Group (WMG:NASDAQ) reported faster streaming growth.

TIKR tracks 41 analysts on Spotify. How many say "Buy"?

See the full breakdown of Buy, Hold, and Sell ratings on Spotify, along with Wall Street's revenue and earnings estimates, all in one place. More than 500,000 investors use TIKR to research stocks like this one. See Spotify's Analyst Ratings

Price did the heavy lifting

Spotify added 6 million Premium subscribers in the third quarter, 1 million above guidance. Premium revenue grew 17%, nearly twice as fast as subscribers, and gross margin hit a third-quarter record of 33.0%.

Operating expenses rose 26%, though, holding the operating margin to 13.5%. Co-CEO Alex Norström said Spotify's "costs are moderating, and there is more runway ahead." Its fourth-quarter guide of €820 million of operating income, a 15.8% margin, also topped Wall Street's estimate.

Analysts expect normalized EPS to rise about 45% from 2025 to 2027:

Spotify Technology (SPOT): normalized EPS, actual and consensus estimates, $ per share, fiscal 2024-2029 (TIKR)
AI gives subscribers something new to pay for

Premium revenue per user grew 7.5% at constant currency in the third quarter. Management guides 4.5% to 5% for the fourth quarter as Spotify laps price increases in more than 150 markets.

On Oct. 30, the Financial Times reported that Spotify plans a paid AI remix and cover service for early 2027. It could cost $4 to $5 a month extra. Universal Music Group has reportedly signed, but Sony Music and Warner haven't.

Warner has leverage. Its recorded-music subscription streaming growth sped up to 15% last quarter. Warner credits that partly to higher per-subscriber minimums from streaming services. It also lists AI licensing among its drivers for fiscal 2027. Whether it signs, and at what royalty, decides how much of that $4 to $5 Spotify keeps.

title: Warner Music: 3 Key Takeaways for Long-Term Investors
detail:
Warner Music: 3 Key Takeaways for Long-Term Investors
The Motley Fool Team, The Motley Fool
Thu, November 19, 2026 at 1:07 PM CST 3 min read
SPOT
WMG
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

On its fourth-quarter 2026 earnings call, held on Nov. 19, 2026, Warner Music (NASDAQ:WMG) reported an all-time high annual revenue, driven by accelerating subscription streaming. Contractual price increases with streaming partners and expanding operational margins show the music publisher is turning structural industry shifts into durable cash flows. Discipline in talent investments and new digital licensing models position it well for multiyear expansion. Three things management said stand out.

1. Contractual Price Increases Fuel Streaming Acceleration

Warner Music negotiates per-subscriber minimum (PSM) rate floors with major digital service provider (DSP) platforms, such as Spotify and Apple Music, to ensure a guaranteed baseline price. These contractual uplifts drove subscription streaming revenue up 15% in the fourth quarter.

In Q4, total revenue increased 7%, led by an acceleration in Recorded Music subscription streaming growth to 15%. This performance was bolstered by the successful implementation of contractual PSM increases across several of our major DSP partners and continued market share gains in most of our major operating regions.
-- Robert Kyncl, CEO

2. Cost Discipline Drives Margin Expansion Past Targets

Operating efficiency initiatives helped Warner Music widen its full-year adjusted operating income before depreciation and amortization (OIBDA, a metric of core operational profit) margin by 210 basis points, surpassing its annual guidance target. Transforming operations from a traditional holding structure into a technology-driven operating business provides lasting leverage.

The expansion is really driven by several items, our strategic reorganization and the ongoing cost management efforts, including the savings we've realized from the restructuring plan, which will continue into '27.
-- Louis Dickler, acting CFO

3. Generative AI Partnerships Unlock New Royalty Streams

Rather than resisting generative artificial intelligence (AI) tools, Warner Music is pioneering licensing frameworks that capture royalties when AI services use its catalog. Securing commercial agreements with creation platforms establishes a key monetization model as user interactivity expands across digital channels.

As a result of our partnership, in September, following the launch of its latest model, Suno became the first of what will be many generative AI companies paying revenue to rights holders.
-- Robert Kyncl, CEO

Looking Ahead

Operational leverage and guaranteed minimum pricing models provide Warner Music with a predictable foundation for growth. Digital subscription renewals, catalog investments, and artificial intelligence licensing will drive cash conversion.

Netflix Is 48% Below Its High While Guiding to Record Revenue of $51.1 Billion, Up 13%, for 2026 ©cottonbro studio from Pexels, Anastasia Shuraeva from Pexels via Canva
Key Takeaways

Netflix hit a new 52-week low this week, 48% below its high a year ago, while guiding 2026 revenue to a record $51.1 billion.

Analysts expect 10.8% revenue growth and a 33.3% operating margin in 2027; the stock is priced as if they're wrong.

Netflix's content cash is outrunning amortization, Disney wants higher streaming margins, and Spotify expects slower growth in revenue per user.

The selloff looks overdone, and January's 2027 guidance will test that.

Netflix (NFLX:NASDAQ) hit a new 52-week low on Nov. 17. At $59.82, the stock sits 48% below its $115.25 high from Nov. 18, 2025.

That's a lot of pessimism for a company guiding to record revenue. The bet is that Netflix's price increases are running out of road. That hits Spotify (SPOT:NYSE), which leans on them too, and matters for Walt Disney (DIS:NYSE), still chasing the margins Netflix already earns.

Netflix's Slowdown Is Real, and So Is the Guide

Revenue growth slowed from 17.6% in the fourth quarter of 2025 to 11.8% in the third quarter of 2026, with 11.5% guided for the fourth. U.S. and Canada revenue grew 11%, inside the 8% to 13% range of March's U.S. price increases. Churn still improved year over year, so members took the higher prices and stayed.

Analysts expect 10.8% growth in 2027 and 9.9% in 2028:

NFLX Revenue, Actual and Consensus Estimates: 2023-2028 (TIKR)

Spotify guides Premium revenue per user to grow 4.5% to 5% in the fourth quarter, down from 7.5% at constant currency. Yet Spotify trades at about 39x forward earnings, more than double Netflix. That's a wide gap for two companies pulling the same lever.

Earnings Keep Climbing if the Margin Holds

Consensus has earnings per share rising to $4.51 by 2028:

NFLX Normalized EPS, Actual and Consensus Estimates: 2023-2028 (TIKR)

The 2026 estimate of $3.57 includes the one-time $2.8 billion Warner Bros. Discovery termination fee from the first quarter, so 2027's growth looks smaller than it is. Analysts expect operating income to rise 17% in 2027, to $18.9 billion, on a 33.3% margin, up from this year's 31.5% guide.

TIKR Tracks 51 Analysts on Netflix. How Many Say "Buy"?

See the full breakdown of Buy, Hold, and Sell ratings on Netflix, along with Wall Street's revenue and earnings estimates, all in one place. More than 500,000 investors use TIKR to research stocks like this one. See Netflix's Analyst Ratings

The margin is the weak spot. Netflix paid $15.0 billion for content in the first nine months of 2026, up 18.5%, while amortization rose 9.5% to $12.8 billion. Most of it hits expenses within four years of each title's release.

Disney shows how hard that margin is to earn. Its Disney+ and Hulu subscription business posted an 11.5% operating margin for fiscal 2026. Bloomberg Intelligence senior media analyst Geetha Ranganathan asked on a Bloomberg podcast this week: "can we get to those 30% margins that Netflix has shown us? I mean, that's the big question."

Spotify (SPOT) has been one of the most searched-for stocks on Zacks.com lately. So, you might want to look at some of the facts that could shape the stock's performance in the near term.

Over the past month, shares of this music-streaming service operator have returned +16.3%, compared to the Zacks S&P 500 composite's -2.4% change. During this period, the Zacks Internet - Software industry, which Spotify falls in, has lost 10.6%. The key question now is: What could be the stock's future direction?

Although media reports or rumors about a significant change in a company's business prospects usually cause its stock to trend and lead to an immediate price change, there are always certain fundamental factors that ultimately drive the buy-and-hold decision.

Earnings Estimate Revisions

Here at Zacks, we prioritize appraising the change in the projection of a company's future earnings over anything else. That's because we believe the present value of its future stream of earnings is what determines the fair value for its stock.

We essentially look at how sell-side analysts covering the stock are revising their earnings estimates to reflect the impact of the latest business trends. And if earnings estimates go up for a company, the fair value for its stock goes up. A higher fair value than the current market price drives investors' interest in buying the stock, leading to its price moving higher. This is why empirical research shows a strong correlation between trends in earnings estimate revisions and near-term stock price movements.

For the current quarter, Spotify is expected to post earnings of $3.71 per share, indicating a change of -28.1% from the year-ago quarter. The Zacks Consensus Estimate has changed +0.7% over the last 30 days.

The consensus earnings estimate of $13.6 for the current fiscal year indicates a year-over-year change of +14.4%. This estimate has changed -1.2% over the last 30 days.

For the next fiscal year, the consensus earnings estimate of $15.86 indicates a change of +16.6% from what Spotify is expected to report a year ago. Over the past month, the estimate has changed -8.6%.

Having a strong externally audited track record, our proprietary stock rating tool, the Zacks Rank, offers a more conclusive picture of a stock's price direction in the near term, since it effectively harnesses the power of earnings estimate revisions. Due to the size of the recent change in the consensus estimate, along with three other factors related to earnings estimates, Spotify is rated Zacks Rank #3 (Hold).

title: Is Spotify (SPOT) a Buy as Wall Street Analysts Look Optimistic?
detail:
Is Spotify (SPOT) a Buy as Wall Street Analysts Look Optimistic?
Zacks Equity Research
November 9, 2026 4 min read
SPOT
Trade SPOT on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Investors often turn to recommendations made by Wall Street analysts before making a Buy, Sell, or Hold decision about a stock. While media reports about rating changes by these brokerage-firm employed (or sell-side) analysts often affect a stock's price, do they really matter?

Before we discuss the reliability of brokerage recommendations and how to use them to your advantage, let's see what these Wall Street heavyweights think about Spotify (SPOT).

Spotify currently has an average brokerage recommendation (ABR) of 1.76, on a scale of 1 to 5 (Strong Buy to Strong Sell), calculated based on the actual recommendations (Buy, Hold, Sell, etc.) made by 35 brokerage firms. An ABR of 1.76 approximates between Strong Buy and Buy.

Of the 35 recommendations that derive the current ABR, 21 are Strong Buy and three are Buy. Strong Buy and Buy respectively account for 60% and 8.6% of all recommendations.

Brokerage Recommendation Trends for SPOT
Broker Rating Breakdown Chart for SPOT

Check price target & stock forecast for Spotify here>>>

While the ABR calls for buying Spotify, it may not be wise to make an investment decision solely based on this information. Several studies have shown limited to no success of brokerage recommendations in guiding investors to pick stocks with the best price increase potential.

Are you wondering why? The vested interest of brokerage firms in a stock they cover often results in a strong positive bias of their analysts in rating it. Our research shows that for every "Strong Sell" recommendation, brokerage firms assign five "Strong Buy" recommendations.

This means that the interests of these institutions are not always aligned with those of retail investors, giving little insight into the direction of a stock's future price movement. It would therefore be best to use this information to validate your own analysis or a tool that has proven to be highly effective at predicting stock price movements.

Zacks Rank, our proprietary stock rating tool with an impressive externally audited track record, categorizes stocks into five groups, ranging from Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy) to Zacks Rank #5 (Strong Sell), and is an effective indicator of a stock's price performance in the near future. Therefore, using the ABR to validate the Zacks Rank could be an efficient way of making a profitable investment decision.

Zacks Rank Should Not Be Confused With ABR

In spite of the fact that Zacks Rank and ABR both appear on a scale from 1 to 5, they are two completely different measures.

Broker recommendations are the sole basis for calculating the ABR, which is typically displayed in decimals (such as 1.28). The Zacks Rank, on the other hand, is a quantitative model designed to harness the power of earnings estimate revisions. It is displayed in whole numbers -- 1 to 5.
